newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says awaits word on Bre-X, Barrick deal.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says awaits word on Bre-X, Barrick deal.

text.p: Indonesian officials remained uncertain on Monday about a split of the huge Busang gold find, with Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana saying he was in the dark over the deal between two Canadian companies.

The ministry's secretary-general Umar Said said last week mining companies Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp had made a joint submission in which they agreed on a 22.5-67.5 percent split of the Busang find in East Kalimantan province.
The remaining 10 percent would go to the government, Umar said.
When asked on Monday whether he had received a letter from Bre-X on the deal, Sudjana told journalists: "Nothing has come to me up till now."
"What should I say?...They haven't reported to me yet. If they do, I will ask them to make an announcement (of their deal), that you have a deal with each other," he said.
Asked if the companies had to report their agreement, Sudjana said: "If they don't report, when are they going to sign the contract. It's difficult if they don't report."
"We are hoping that this project will get under way soon. I'm left waiting for them," he said.
Bre-X estimates the Busang discovery contains at least 57 million ounces of gold currently worth around $21 billion.
On the 10 percent stake sought by the government in Busang, the minister said: "We will later bring out the funds and invest as well." He did not elaborate.
A source close to the Bre-X/Barrick negotiations said last week the two companies had agreed on the division of the Busang II and III sections of the property which contain the bulk of the gold.
Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said a week ago: "We have made a submission...which says we can work together if the government can satisfy requests by both parties on a couple of items."
The source close to the negotiations said Bre-X and Barrick had agreed on financial terms to give the latter a major stake to develop the find, but the terms were not disclosed.
